title: The AWS CLI: profiles, named accounts and CloudShell

videos.script: Every lesson so far has typed commands into a terminal with three variables set. This lesson opens the rest of the command line's settings. {{files}} There are two files in your home directory. One holds keys, the other holds everything else, and a profile is a name that groups settings in both. {{layers}} The command line reads its settings from three places. The command itself wins, then the environment, then the files. You will measure that with the region, and get three answers to one question. {{exception}} Credentials have one exception, and this lab depends on it. Naming a profile with a variable loses to the keys in the environment. Naming it with an option wins. {{role}} Then a profile that assumes a role in another account on every command, so one laptop can work in six accounts without editing anything. {{query}} And last, how to shape what comes back: a query that picks the fields, four ways to print them, and the pages the command line follows for you. {{end}}
